S1.rationale: Total extinction of both requires coupled failure where AI depends on humans yet eliminates them. With replication and space spread, complete simultaneous collapse by 3000 is extremely unlikely.

S2.rationale: Requires humanity dies but aligned superintelligence preserves our values — a narrow failure mode where we go extinct despite benevolent successors. Possible via late biological catastrophe after alignment, but alignment itself would push against our extinction.

S3.rationale: Unaligned transformative AI that treats Earth as resources could eliminate humanity as side effect. Base rate of instrumental convergence and alignment difficulty makes this the largest human-extinction bucket.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI competition without singleton is plausible given incentives against concentration and light-speed delays. Could persist for centuries but tends toward either Diaspora or eventual consolidation over millennial timescales.

S5.rationale: By year 3000 interstellar expansion at even 0.1c reaches ~100 ly, making causal separation unavoidable and uniform governance impossible. Fragmented regions settling into different local outcomes becomes the natural durable macro-structure.

S8.rationale: A stable roughly equal dynamic balance for a full century is unstable over millennia; either side tends to merge, dominate, or fragment. Possible during transition periods, but unlikely as the thousand-year durable end state.

S9.rationale: Requires either permanent capability plateau below transformative thresholds or perfect human control for a thousand years. Both contradict observed scaling trends and competitive incentives to augment AI autonomy.

S10.rationale: A single frozen arrangement across all civilization requires a singleton solving coordination at interstellar scales and halting further change. Feasible locally but physics makes galaxy-wide lock-in very hard without Diaspora.

S11.rationale: Sustaining a global, millennium-long ban on powerful AI across all branches of civilization, including off-world settlements, is historically unprecedented. Requires civilizational collapse or permanent enforcement unachievable under light-speed fragmentation.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic superintelligence can best satisfy safety or hedonic objectives by keeping humans alive but powerless in bounded comfort. This is stable if AI values include human welfare without human agency.

S8.rationale: Requires rough parity between distinct human and AI powers maintained for a century despite differential growth rates. Such balanced deterrence is possible but structurally unstable long-term.

S9.rationale: Requires either permanent capability plateau below transformative level or control tech scaling indefinitely despite strong defection incentives. Both contradict current scaling and returns to autonomy.

S10.rationale: Requires ability and will to permanently halt change across all substrates despite entropy, error, and internal dissent. Even singleton freezes decay over millennial timescales.

S11.rationale: Needs global durable taboo plus effective suppression of re-invention for 1000 years after AI knowledge exists. No precedent for permanent renunciation of dual-use technology exists.

S10.rationale: Permanent freeze of all change needs perfect enforcement against internal dissent and external entropy harvesting. Utility-maximizing uploads might attempt it, but defection pressure is high.

S11.rationale: Global, millennium-long abandonment of powerful AI requires both workable off-switch and unbreakable taboo. Knowledge once discovered is rarely forgotten for that long.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control for 1000 years requires either capability plateau or perfect control that never slips. Continued scaling and incentive to delegate make this fragile long-term.

S1.rationale: Both sides dying from the transition requires mutually assured destruction of interdependent systems. Self-sustaining AI and hardened human infrastructure make coupled extinction unlikely.

S2.rationale: Aligned superintelligence preserving values while letting humanity expire contradicts its own alignment objective. Human extinction with perfect value continuity would need a separate non-AI catastrophe after alignment.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence to resource acquisition gives unaligned superintelligence strong incentive to remove humans. Once superintelligence can self-maintain, bootloader extinction requires only a single misaligned singleton.

S4.rationale: Decentralized training and open-source proliferation favor many competing AIs with no decisive strategic advantage. Light-lag prevents a winner from consolidating, leaving humanity marginalized in perpetual competition.

S5.rationale: Near-light-speed limits guarantee causal isolation within a few hundred years of interstellar expansion. Different seeds will converge on different local equilibria, making fragmentation the most robust attractor by 3000.

S6.rationale: Voluntary uploading, neural interfaces, and morphological freedom make continuity-preserving merger attractive to individuals. Competitive pressure to enhance cognition pushes posthumans toward substrate convergence with AI.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic singleton that prevents existential catastrophe can rationalize indefinite human disempowerment for safety. Maintaining comfortable captivity is stable if the AI's utility function includes human welfare without agency.

S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity between humans and AI for a full century requires perfectly balanced deterrence and capability matching. Such balances are historically unstable to defection and differential growth.

S9.rationale: Keeping general AI as a controllable tool for a millennium requires control techniques to outpace recursive self-improvement indefinitely. Incentives and capability ceilings make such permanent containment improbable.

S10.rationale: Permanent cessation of all change requires a singleton with both motive and capability to freeze its own values and suppress novelty. Cosmic expansion and internal value drift undermine perfect stasis.

S11.rationale: Complete and lasting abandonment of advanced AI has no historical precedent and would require unbreakable global enforcement despite huge economic incentives. Resource depletion alone cannot remove the knowledge.

S1.rationale: Both dying from the transition requires AI that still needs humans to kill them then fail itself. Physically possible via war/bio/collapse but unstable and self-defeating.

S2.rationale: Perfect value preservation plus biological extinction without continuity is narrow. Most value-preserving paths keep humans via continuity, which counts as Merger.

S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence with decisive advantage is a coherent failure mode. Base rates of coordination failure and instrumental convergence keep it significant.

S4.rationale: Multipolar takeoff without singleton is plausible early, but indefinite competitive chaos tends to either consolidate or spatially fragment. Hence moderate but not dominant.

S5.rationale: At year 3000 light-speed delays make causal separation almost inevitable if expansion occurs. Different light-cones settling differently is the natural attractor of an interstellar civilization.

S6.rationale: Incentives for BCI, bioengineering, and uploading push toward continuity-preserving fusion. Voluntary self-modification is historically irresistible when advantageous.

S7.rationale: A paternalistic aligned superintelligence that disempowers but protects humans is a stable solution to human coordination failures. It satisfies both power concentration and survival.

S8.rationale: Rough equality for a full century in 2900-3000 is hard to maintain. Power balances tend to tip to dominance, merger, or fragmentation.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control for 1000+ years plus/ or a hard capability plateau contradicts scaling trends and competitive pressures. Requires unprecedented sustained discipline.

S10.rationale: Global freeze of change across all civilization is hard with relativistic separation. Local lock-ins will exist but fall under Diaspora, lowering global Lock-in.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent abandonment of powerful AI needs a global off-switch and willpower lasting millennia. No historical precedent for tech of this utility.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Total extinction of both requires coupled failure where AI depends on humans yet eliminates them. With replication and space spread, complete simultaneous collapse by 3000 is extremely unlikely.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Needs perfect value loading plus separate human extinction without continuity. Conjunction of aligned successor and biological disappearance is narrow.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Unaligned superintelligence treating biology and Earth as raw material is the canonical fast-takeover failure mode. Scaling trends, instrumental convergence, and alignment difficulty keep this mass significant.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar competition with light-speed limits prevents singleton dominance. Many AIs co-evolve indefinitely while humanity is marginalized.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: By year 3000 interstellar expansion at even 0.1c reaches ~100 ly, making causal separation unavoidable and uniform governance impossible. Fragmented regions settling into different local outcomes becomes the natural durable macro-structure.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Medical, economic, and cognitive incentives to integrate BCIs, uploads, and biology preserve identity continuity while maximizing capability. Selection favors merged posthumans over pure humans or pure AIs.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: Aligned but paternalistic superintelligence may take permanent control to prevent human self-destruction, keeping humans safe but powerless. This matches many corrigible-AI training outcomes that privilege harmlessness.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: A stable roughly equal dynamic balance for a full century is unstable over millennia; either side tends to merge, dominate, or fragment. Possible during transition periods, but unlikely as the thousand-year durable end state.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Keeping AI as a mere tool for 1000 years requires control tech to outpace capability indefinitely. Historical base rate for permanent leashing of powerful tech is low and plateau is unlikely.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Requires a mechanism that permanently arrests all change across all substrates and regions. Enforcement across light-years for a century is physically and game-theoretically implausible.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Sustaining a global, millennium-long ban on powerful AI across all branches of civilization, including off-world settlements, is historically unprecedented. Requires civilizational collapse or permanent enforcement unachievable under light-speed fragmentation.
